User-visible claims & geometry mismatches:
1. Notation Swap: In the textbook, $p_i$ represents the observed image coordinate and $p'_i$ represents the estimated projection under current camera parameters ($p'_i = \pi(K[R|-RT]P_i)$). The generated figure swaps this: $p_i$ is placed on the projection ray (making it the estimated projection), and $p'_i$ is the displaced point (making it the observed/detected point).
2. Parameter Coupling Mismatch: In the simulation, adjusting the 'Sensor Noise' slider moves the ray-aligned point $p_i$ (which represents the estimated projection), while adjusting the 'Calibration Error' slider moves the off-ray point $p'_i$ (representing the observed sensor measurement). Geometrically, calibration error should shift the camera model's projected rays ($p'_i$), while sensor noise simulates measurement uncertainty in the static detected points ($p_i$). This is backwards and highly confusing for students attempting to link the visual geometry with the formulas.
gemini-3.5-flash.concept_accuracy_improvement: Swap the roles of $p_i$ and $p'_i$ to match the textbook notation (where $p_i$ is the detected/observed measurement and $p'_i$ is the projected estimate).
